title: Welcome to Rotli
body:
# Welcome to Rotli

This is a real Markdown note in your vault. Edit it, experiment here, or delete it when you no longer need it.

## Things to try

1. Change this sentence. Rotli saves as you type: the small dot above the note dims while you write and fills in again once the change is on disk. There is nothing to press.
2. Press **⌘T** to create a note, or **⌘N** to choose what a new tab becomes.
3. Press **⌘K** to search notes, files, chats, and actions.
4. Type `/` on an empty line to explore Markdown blocks.
5. Press **⌥A** to open Chat and ask about one of your notes.
6. Drop an image or file into **Assets**.

## Guided lessons

Not sure what New, Main, or Aa do? Settings → General → **Show me around** runs a short tour that points at each one.

The **Welcome** folder in Main holds three short lessons: **Writing**, **Organizing and finding**, and **AI and privacy**. Each one is an ordinary note with room to make mistakes. Click a control, then choose **Aa → Raw markdown** to see the same text underneath, and **Beautified** to return.

Edit the lessons, or delete the folder when you are done. Settings → General → Open welcome folder brings it back.

- [ ] Try a lesson
- [ ] Inspect its Markdown
- [ ] Delete what you do not need

## Your vault

- Your files stay in the folder you chose and work in other apps.
- **Library** is where Rotli organizes lasting notes.
- **Assets**, **Archive**, and **Trash** are system views of this same vault.
- This welcome note sits at the vault root, outside Library.

## When you're done

- [ ] I can create, edit, find, rename, trash, and restore a note
- [ ] I know Main and named views refer to the same files
- [ ] I know the Welcome folder is mine to edit or delete

Make it yours.

title: Writing
body:
# Writing

Replace this sentence with something you want to remember. Type `/` on a blank line for headings, lists, tables, and code, and choose **Aa → Raw markdown** any time to see the plain text underneath (**Beautified** returns).

## Make it readable

This is **bold**, this is *italic*, and this is `literal code`.

> A useful note starts with one clear thought.

- Capture the idea
- Keep related thoughts together

1. Choose one next step

## Tasks and results

- [ ] Write the first draft
- [/] Review the details
- [x] Make room to think

Type `[]`, `[/]`, or `[x]` then Space on a fresh line. A result is a pass-or-fail answer; type `[True][False]` then Space, and add `:color` after a label to color it.

- [True:green][Draw:yellow][False:red] What was the outcome?

## Choices and switches

Adjacent circles make one choice (`[#]`); squares under a question pick several (`[##?]`, then `[##]`); `[|]` is a switch.

- [#] Small
- [#x] Medium
- [#] Large

- [##?] What belongs in the first release?
- [##x] Writing
- [##] Advanced workflows

- [True:green|x False:red] Ready to share
- [:blue|:green] A color-only switch

## Tables and code

Type `| Step | Owner |` on a fresh line and press Enter; Rotli adds the divider row for you.

| Step | Owner | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft | Me | Ready |
| Share | Me | Later |

```ts
const nextStep = "Write one useful note";
```

Inside code, `[#]`, `[True|False]`, and `- [ ]` stay literal text.

title: Organizing and finding
body:
# Organizing and finding

## Links

Create a note titled **My first idea** (⌘T), come back, type `[[`, and pick it from the list. Click the link to open it; rename that note and the old title still resolves.

- [ ] Link to My first idea
- [ ] Find it with ⌘K search

## Main and named views

This lesson sits in Main → Welcome and in All notes: two ways to reach one file. Use the **Main ▾** picker at the top of Main to make a named view and add this note to it. Removing a note from Main keeps the file; Trash is a separate step you can undo.

- [ ] Make a named view and add this note
- [ ] Remove the view and find the note in All notes

## Files and attachments

These make real files, so start with disposable examples.

- [ ] New → Document or Board: add something, close, and reopen
- [ ] Attach an image to this note and resize it

title: AI and privacy
body:
# AI and privacy

Writing works without a model. Chat and the Librarian are optional capabilities.

Use only disposable sample text for these checks. Connect a provider only when you choose to.

- [ ] Write and find a note while offline
- [ ] Review the Librarian setting and its explanation
- [ ] Create a secure test note and confirm remote AI cannot read it
- [ ] Lock a test note and confirm AI cannot edit it
- [ ] Inspect a saved chat as ordinary Markdown

Secure is an AI access boundary, not encryption at rest. Locked notes remain readable. Browser tests cannot prove Keychain, a provider's live behavior, or scheduled delivery.
